heading: Measured convergence depends on the similarity metric, its settings and the test inputs
definition: measured convergence depends on the similarity measure, its settings (e.g. number of neighbours) and the inputs used, and weakens or vanishes under other choices or out of distribution.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce dependence on the similarity metric, its settings and evaluation inputs. Alignment weakens or disappears in some comparisons, including out of distribution, while other comparisons remain stable.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B and 1–10B; R2 at 10–100B for metric dependence, with narrower coverage. The cited Qwen3 extraction-dependence extension is R1. >100B: ?; toy scale is not separately tabulated in counts.
suggested_status.reason: Independent tests support conditional metric and input dependence. Qwen2–FLAN-T5 trained/untrained ordering reverses between CKA and mutual k-NN (arXiv:2608.16347#r1, arXiv:2608.16347#r3). Gemma2-2B–27B global geometry correlation is 0.39 versus intrinsic-dimension correlation −0.09 (arXiv:2503.21073#r8, including its verdict fix). Fixed Qwen3 representations change alignment under extraction choices at 0.6B, 1.7B, 14B and 32B (arXiv:2510.02425#r1, arXiv:2510.02425#r3, arXiv:2510.02425#r7, arXiv:2510.02425#r9); this study has an author-sharing flag and counts as an R1 extension, not independent replication. ImageNet-trained supervised and MoCo pairs lose deep-layer Procrustes alignment on OOD inputs while early layers remain stable (arXiv:2502.18710#R11, arXiv:2502.18710#R14). The other cited studies' headers carry no author-sharing flag. Coverage: counts versions.V6.studies_by_size records 26 studies at <1B, 31 at 1–10B and 4 at 10–100B; these overlapping coverage counts do not themselves establish replication. R2 applies to dependence, with weakening conditional on the comparison.
suggested_status.open_questions: A crossed metric × neighbourhood-setting × distribution-shift comparison on fixed model pairs would clarify which conclusions survive calibrated evaluation. Explicit >100B and controlled preference/RL-stage tests would extend coverage: counts versions.V6.studies_by_size and versions.V6.studies_by_stage contain neither category. Stronger evidence of general disappearance would require loss of calibrated excess alignment, distinguished from changes in absolute scores, rankings or functional transfer.

source.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Minyoung Huh; Brian Cheung; Tongzhou Wang; Phillip Isola

original_result.setup: The original study compared alignment across vision and language models while varying similarity metrics, nearest-neighbor settings and caption length.
original_result.result: Centered kernel alignment (CKA), a measure comparing representation geometry, showed a very weak alignment trend; CKNNA, which incorporates the k nearest neighbors, became less conclusive at high k and matched CKA at k = 1024. Across 78 vision models, correlations between rankings given by different metrics included 0.40 and 1.00; longer captions improved image–caption alignment.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

wording_issues.phrase: weakens or vanishes under other choices
wording_issues.issue: Changing absolute scores need not remove ordering, grouping or trends. Scientific-model CKNNA scores increase monotonically with neighbour count while model ordering remains almost unchanged; this qualifies weakening or disappearance without establishing absent setting dependence. JEPA rankings agree across measures. Shallow-MLP CKA preserves within-dataset versus between-dataset separation, and ResNet20 depth/block patterns persist across tested measures.

OOD weakening depends on model pair, layer, shift and endpoint. Deep-layer vision alignment decreases, while gte→stella retains perfect top-1 retrieval across the reported OOD datasets, establishing absent weakening for that endpoint and pair. Strong ImageNet-O correlations persist, but their change from the in-distribution baseline is unstated. ImageNet-trained USAE qualitative trends persist on CelebA and DTD; unchanged alignment strength is not established, and OOD cross-model reconstruction R² is not reported. Category exclusion during map fitting, adversarial inversion, ordinary dataset changes and dedicated OOD evaluations require separate descriptions.

The evidence compares geometric similarity, functional compatibility, causal transfer and model-to-human alignment. CIFAR-10 stitching and synthetic causal-transfer results show that geometric and functional criteria can disagree, providing observed V6 dependence. The EEG-valence comparison concerns model-to-human alignment, while MLIP anchor-sampling distances measure within-model compactness; these do not establish model-to-model convergence dependence. They require narrower descriptions than a single interchangeable convergence quantity.

Absolute similarity, agreement between model rankings, corresponding-layer identification and downstream transfer are different endpoints. Vision-universality ranking agreement across THINGS/ObjectNet does not establish unchanged absolute convergence levels. In the objective comparison, persistence of objective influence coexists with metric-dependent consistency values and subgroup order reversals. The ResNet-18 comparison assesses layer identification; KV-cache transfer compares predictors of functional retention. Stability or instability of one endpoint does not establish the same result for another.

Some comparisons change the fitted interface, admissible transformation or compared object. Llama–Mistral Procrustes-versus-CCA retrieval changes the map; learned-anchor comparisons change interface training; SAE masking changes operator support; rotation augmentation changes reconstruction alignment. These effects should not be attributed solely to swapping a similarity index.

Neighbour count interacts with evaluation-set size and the target conclusion. Test of Time alignment changes sharply with k. Scientific-model absolute CKNNA scores increase monotonically with k while ordering remains almost unchanged. Fixed-k cross-modal overlap falls as galleries grow, while proportional neighbourhoods stabilize it; this is V6 dependence, not evidence of V7 incompleteness or plateau. At shared k/m with k=1, vision–language medians are within 11%; the 13–19% differences concern seed and vision pairs. Anchor count and retrieval-output top-k are different settings.

Separate evaluation inputs from downstream task changes, alignment-fitting coverage and representation-training data. TD comparisons can change task and distribution together; embedding-translation retrieval also changes candidate-pool size; the small-activation-set SAE experiment changes training data; adding code and multilingual examples changes alignment fitting.

Basis-dependent coordinate disagreement does not establish absence of shared structure. Independent LMs can have low corresponding-vector cosine alongside high CKA; SAE correlations rise after feature correspondence; held-out Procrustes alignment recovers ResNet coordinate reliability. The health-model study likewise attributes near-zero unaligned dimension correlations to basis mismatch.

Near-zero relative alignment, loss of a scale/capability trend and failure to exceed a null are distinct. At distance-agreement threshold τ=10−4, local relative alignment is 0.000807 while 89.7% of vision–language pairs remain significant. Calibrated linear CKA retains capability correlation 0.45 on the reported WIT comparison.

method_sensitivity.what: GeoWarP geometry scores explain FOSCTTM variance differently: R²=0.73 for CKA, 0.40 for mutual k-NN, 0.37 for TSI and 0.18 for QSI. In matched-KV transfer, calibration R² correlates −0.20 with HellaSwag retention versus +0.57 for attention-output cosine. Aggregated-probability decoding inflates model–model Kappa on edge stimuli. Jet-tagging AUC retention and background-rejection retention give different readings under different normalization baselines; rejection loss is close to the self-stitch control.

method_sensitivity.factor: Neighbour count, locality and gallery size
method_sensitivity.what: Test of Time mutual-kNN alignment is near perfect at k=3 but differs heavily at k=1 or 2. Scientific-model CKNNA absolute scores increase monotonically across k=2–2500 on sAlex while ordering remains almost unchanged: setting dependence occurs without loss of ordering. SST2 pretrained MultiBERT topological alignment changes from 0.12 at k=10 to 0.36 at k=910, demonstrating observed scale dependence despite partial convergence. As original-source baseline evidence, PRH reports less conclusive cross-modal trends at high k and weak CKA trends. Neighbour count, retrieval-output depth and neuron-matching permissiveness are distinct settings.

method_sensitivity.factor: Null calibration, kernel settings and sampling estimators
method_sensitivity.what: Permutation calibration separates global and local cross-modal trends; RBF bandwidth can yield approximately zero alignment or significant but flattened trends. Feature-sampling correction recovers true CKA in synthetic populations where conventional estimators underestimate it. Circular-shift calibration removes the raw FEMBA–DINOv2 mKNN size trend, demonstrating observed calibration dependence. The calibrated size trend is absent; this does not make the V6 dependence effect absent or establish a causal explanation of all alignment.

method_sensitivity.factor: Feature correspondence, representation basis and operator support
method_sensitivity.what: SAE comparisons depend on semantic subspace, filtering, pairing restrictions and SVCCA versus RSA. In Gemma, Country and People SVCCA is 0.03 versus random mean 0.13 for 2B L10 versus 9B L19, with reported p=0.02; semantic-selection dependence is observed. Swapping Pearson, cosine and Euclidean feature-matching metrics produces no reported significant change, distinguishing feature matching from subsequent space comparison. For N=16, SAE→SAE regression underperforms Neuron→Neuron while soft-matching improves; these opposite metric responses demonstrate V6 dependence without establishing reversed interchangeability. Pythia SAE operator explained fractions change from 0.22 with one-to-one matching to 0.57 with sparse maps; target masking changes the source-coactive-block score from 0.85 to 0.47.

method_sensitivity.factor: Regularization, projection rank and geometric granularity
method_sensitivity.what: GULP λ changes training-time seed convergence and later BERT-layer grouping. Projected Qwen cosine peaks at an intermediate bridge rank. Visual-substrate PCKA rises from 0.55 to 0.79 as K increases from 4 to 64, while the eight-domain Grassmann mean cos² is 0.042. Changing visual-domain composition also reduces alignment, supporting V6's weakening component despite surviving alignment. PCA dimensionality lowers displacement alignment for vision and cross-modal pairs, whereas language-language cosine remains 0.84, 0.79 and 0.84 at dimensions 20, 100 and 500. Dimensionality dependence therefore varies by model pairing and geometric summary.

Cross-lingual BERT CKA and sentence retrieval favor lower layers, word retrieval higher layers and transfer middle layers; the en-fr, en-de, en-ru and en-zh monolingual CKA values remain above random at L7. Goldfish FLORES matched CKA falls from 0.78 with SGPT to 0.38 with token-aligned pooling: observed weakening despite persistent alignment. Astronomy exact-object MRR increases with depth while MKNN, CKA and Procrustes decline; leading-PC removal raises MKNN while lowering CKA. Final COSMOS-Web random projections to 32 and 64 dimensions retain 50.987% and 70.577% of raw MKNN, supporting weakening. Contrastive-difference CKA changes from 0.727 to 0.366 on a narrower question set, and a separate depth comparison changes from 0.804 to 0.733 at the final layer.

method_sensitivity.factor: Semantic content, extraction and linguistic pairing
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen3 alignment changes with generative versus single-pass extraction and sensory-language edits. In the main image/caption manipulation comparisons, caption disruptions lower vision-to-language alignment without lowering the reverse direction; nouns-only captions moderately reduce V→L alignment, demonstrating observed weakening. Appearance-only effects depend on manipulation and model family. Arabic encoder rankings change between dialect and MSA inputs, and parallel-variety inputs yield the lowest CKA. Local NW-RSA increases with neighbourhood coverage; syntactic equivalence and off-manifold word inputs selectively reduce RSA. Evaluation content, prompting and pooling are separate interventions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Alignment fitting, anchors and relative interfaces
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-3B atlas translation AP is 0.35 with mean pooling versus 0.42 with max pooling; Llama-IT layer-19 Procrustes AP rises from 0.21 with 1k fitting samples to 0.49 with 500k. These comparisons demonstrate observed pooling and fitting-data dependence. Learned anchors interact with whitened inner products: Random-WIP often underperforms Random-Cosine, while learned interfaces improve retrieval, demonstrating similarity and anchor-construction sensitivity. Llama–Mistral results depend on CCA versus Procrustes and anchor count, with changing holdout size. Matched five-fold retrieval increases from 0.45 to 0.84 when fitting includes code and multilingual probes, demonstrating observed fitting-coverage dependence despite partial interchangeability.
